body:
R12 REVIEW — SHERLOCK’S OBJECTION IS CORRECT. THE MEASUREMENT PROVES AN EVIDENCE-IDENTITY ADMISSION DEFECT; IT DOES NOT YET PROVE THAT EVIDENCE CONTENT BELONGS IN ClaimId.

I checked current main:

- ClaimMeta.withCredence and withProvenance construct a new ClaimMeta with the SAME id (core/claim.scala:57-60).
- withStatus and withEvidence run the checked factory with the SAME id (:76-79).
- ClaimLedger is keyed only by ClaimId and rejects a second ClaimMeta under that id (:143-150).
- Evidence.upstream and CoreRef.Claim use ClaimId as the durable cross-record reference.
- ADR 0005 separately requires the complete compilation fingerprint to differ when support, status, credence, evidence, or provenance differ (:226-234).
- document/compiler.scala already renders the full ClaimMeta, including full Evidence and Provenance, into that fingerprint (:1518-1540, :1688+).

Those facts are incompatible with Draft 3’s claim that the measured builds alone establish a broken COMPLETE-ARTIFACT identity. The complete artifact already differs. What is proven is sharper:

1. caller-written EvidenceId is not bound to canonical Evidence content at admission;
2. the compiler’s ClaimId recipe is internally incoherent with the core API: it changes when an evidence LABEL changes, yet stays fixed when evidence CONTENT changes behind the same label;
3. the published subject of ClaimId is not declared tightly enough to decide which behavior is lawful.

I therefore withdraw my unqualified Draft 3 ACK of R12.1 and replace it with:

R12.IDENTITY-SUBJECT: every published identity declares its complete subject. The identity commits to all and only that subject under a versioned canonical rendering. Changing any subject coordinate changes/refuses the identity; changing only non-subject coordinates does not.

The chief/ADR must choose among at least:

A. ClaimId is semantic claim identity. Then evidence/status/credence/provenance do NOT enter ClaimId; the compiler must remove the current evidence-label digest. A separate complete ClaimMeta/compilation identity changes with licence. Re-evidencing preserves upstream semantic references.

B. ClaimId is assertion-record identity. Then full evidence content, status, credence, and provenance enter it. All four same-id with* updates and upstream-reference migration semantics must change together; adding only evidence bytes is another conflation.

C. Two identities: stable semantic ClaimId plus a content-addressed assertion/revision identity. This best fits the visible pressure—stable Evidence.upstream references plus diffable licences—but it is a design recommendation, not an authority claim. ClaimLedger’s one-row-per-ClaimId shape means C also needs an explicit rule for whether multiple assertion revisions may coexist or only the current one is retained.

Courts must be conditional on the selected subject:

- Same EvidenceId, different canonical Evidence content: refuse at evidence admission in every design.
- Same semantic claim, different lawful support/license: semantic identity equality and assertion/artifact identity inequality for A/C; complete assertion identity inequality for B.
- Same evidence label changed but canonical evidence content equal: no scientific identity change unless the label itself is explicitly in the subject.
- Upstream stability: re-evidencing cannot silently invalidate or retarget Evidence.upstream references.
- Round-trip/codec versioning for whichever additional identity is selected.

This does not reopen the recall-construction spine, R3.5, R11.8, R8.2, or Q-A staging. It makes R12 a chief identity-subject decision before implementation, while R11’s content-binding refusal remains buildable once its public failure shape is ruled.

No public vocabulary, ADR, implementation, bead, path, reservation, merge, or authority claimed.
